title: The source guide carries no version, date or status in its body
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench How To Read The Acceptance Criteria v1.docx
description: The document body opens with the product name, the title and the line SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group., then goes straight to the reading pattern. It holds no version number, no date, no owner, no status and no change log, so the next version has to take its version from the file name and cannot copy a source date.
evidence: Converted text of the source, paragraphs 1 to 3 and the whole body: no version, date or status line; the file name reads v1
legacy_ref: Recovery Workbench How To Read The Acceptance Criteria v1
proposed: Version 2 dated 22 November 2026 with a metadata table and a change log; version 1 recorded as having no date in the source

title: The guide describes one story per legacy key and gives no way to read a split story
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench How To Read The Acceptance Criteria v1.docx
section: Every user story ends in a set of acceptance criteria
description: The source says every user story ends in a set of acceptance criteria and that every story in the set reads the same way. After D-RCV-60 one legacy key maps to several stories, and the guide has no paragraph on slices, on story keys or on which slice holds which criterion, so a reader who opens a slice cannot tell how it relates to the legacy story.
evidence: Source paragraph 4 and section A worked example; Template and Rules R5.2 and R7.2 introduce story keys per scope and work type and an origin tag on every scenario line
legacy_ref: Recovery Workbench How To Read The Acceptance Criteria v1
proposed: Add How the set is sliced and Reading the slices of one legacy story, and keep every existing section word for word
